# Plan: issue submission base freshness

Report target-branch drift for the exact validated issue checkpoint, retaining the approved base and existing publication fences.

**Shape: Involved.** The Git calculation is small, but submission ordering, fork target selection, structured output, and PR-number-dependent guidance cross several boundaries.

## What we know

- `newSubmitCmd` validates, checks the exact clean head, records/publishes the checkpoint, creates or updates a draft PR, then records submission (`internal/cli/submit.go:126–193`). Freshness belongs after the clean-head check and before checkpoint publication.
- Completed submissions return early; both success paths currently emit a small JSON identity map (`internal/cli/submit.go:89–106`, `:190–193`). Preserve the completed-task shortcut and existing text.
- `formatDraftPRBody` has no PR number parameter (`internal/cli/submit.go:252`). `CreateDraftPR` returns the number; both GitHub and local trackers support `UpdateDraftPR` (`internal/tracker/github.go:612,649`, `internal/tracker/local.go:480,513`). Exact recovery guidance therefore needs an update after creation.
- `origin` is the upstream target; fork publication uses a distinct fork remote (`internal/cli/root.go:116–120`, `internal/workspace/worktree.go:197–221`). Checking the writable fork's tip would inspect the wrong repository.
- `defaultBaseBranch` calls `workspace.ResolveBase`, which fetches and can fail before validation (`internal/cli/submit.go:232`, `internal/workspace/worktree.go:207`). The fetch-failure acceptance criterion must account for this earlier path.
- Hardened coordinator Git commands are available through `gitcredential.Command`; `Output` discards stdout on nonzero exits (`internal/gitcredential/environment.go:59,138`). Merge conflict parsing needs `Command` so exit 1 retains stdout.
- Current command hardening disables configured `filter.*` only for the verbs in its switch; `merge-tree` is absent and custom `merge.*.driver` values are not neutralized (`internal/gitcredential/environment.go:73–108`). Step 1 adds that missing boundary.
- Installed Git is 2.53.0; `git merge-tree -h` advertises `--write-tree`, `--name-only`, `-z`, and `--no-messages`. `make check` runs lint and race tests (Makefile).
- `/swarm-plan` requests these two artifacts only (`.claude/commands/swarm-plan.md`). No source changes or staging/publication are part of this phase.

## What we're assuming

- A local backend without origin should compare the selected local `refs/heads/<base>` directly. Verify with `newCLIFixture` and a local branch that advances independently of the issue worktree.
- Modern merge-tree is available on supported installations. Unsupported Git or an uncomputable merge must produce an informational skipped result, never a false clean result; exercise this with an injected command runner.

## Open questions

- How to discover the default target when the network is unavailable? Step 2 will retain cached origin/HEAD (or the local branch when there is no origin), without silently selecting a different target. If no target name is known, preserve the existing actionable `--base` requirement: publishing cannot proceed without a target branch.
- How does merge-tree behave with custom merge drivers? Step 1 will probe disposable repositories with sentinel commands and add the mandatory neutralization regression test. The mechanism is fixed below: extend hardened command construction, rather than trusting repository-selected commands. If safe inspection cannot be established, report skipped and proceed.
- What if the post-create description update fails? Step 3 prints a sanitized warning saying the PR description lacks the freshness note, includes the exact mode-specific recovery command, then proceeds and records submission. Completed retries remain unchanged and do not repair descriptions. Successful normal submissions contain the exact numbered note.

## Architectural choice

Keep the feature in the CLI submission layer: a small Git inspection helper plus presentation helpers. Do not add lease authority, fork transport operations, background agent work, or changes to `internal/pr.Service.Submit`. An actual merge/rebase would mutate the candidate and is outside scope. A hosting-provider mergeability API would miss local support and does not satisfy the required merge-tree check.

## Files and symbols

- Add `internal/cli/submit_freshness.go`: `submissionFreshness`, `checkSubmissionFreshness`, target-tip resolution, merge-tree parser, and shared advisory/JSON helpers.
- Modify `internal/cli/submit.go`: `newSubmitCmd`, issue-submit default-target resolution, and advisory composition around `formatDraftPRBody`. `defaultBaseBranch` has exactly one caller (`internal/cli/submit.go:81`); change that helper directly for cached-name fallback.
- Modify `internal/gitcredential/environment.go`: `Command` and `appendConfig` usage for merge-tree-specific driver neutralization; retain existing filter protections. Extend `internal/gitcredential/environment_test.go` with sentinel-driver and configuration-probe failure regression tests.
- Add `internal/cli/submit_freshness_test.go`: real disposable Git repositories and focused runner failure tests; reuse `newCLIFixture` and tracker overrides.
- Extend `internal/cli/cli_test.go` fork submission fixtures as needed for upstream-versus-fork coverage; avoid broad fixture rewrites.
- Update the submitting guidance in `docs/developer.md` and the Unreleased section of `CHANGELOG.md`.

## Implementation sequence

1. Build the inspection helper and focused Git fixtures. Resolve/fetch only the selected target (`origin` even in fork mode); use an explicit refspec and `--no-write-fetch-head` to refresh its remote-tracking ref, then pin its SHA. With no origin, resolve the selected local branch. Never consult stale refs after a failed fetch. Extend `gitcredential.Command` with a `merge-tree` case: probe configured driver keys using `git config --null --name-only --get-regexp '^merge\..*\.driver$'` with the hardened environment and existing bounded-output pattern. For every configured custom driver, append command-scoped `GIT_CONFIG_*` overrides via `appendConfig`, setting its driver to the fixed command `false` and its recursive driver to built-in `binary`. Never execute the configured driver value; this conservatively reports a conflict for files requiring a custom driver. Treat probe/configuration errors as skipped. Preserve credential config entries and do not change persistent config. Verify sentinel non-execution before integrating. Use hardened Git commands and a bounded inspection context. Do not touch HEAD, index, worktree files, approved state, or approvals.
2. Compare the pinned target SHA to approved `BaseSHA`. Equality returns a silent unchanged result. Otherwise count `git rev-list --count <base>..<tip>` and run `git merge-tree --write-tree --name-only -z --no-messages <tip> <validated-head>`. Parse the tree record and NUL-delimited conflict paths; exit 0 is clean, exit 1 is conflict, other failures are skipped/unknown. Deduplicate/sort paths and escape them for human/Markdown output. Use generic sanitized skip reasons, not raw command diagnostics. Keep different-tip/zero-count cases honest rather than claiming the target is ahead. Ensure default branch discovery does not turn the advisory fetch failure into an earlier fatal fetch error when a cached target name exists.
3. Integrate immediately after successful validation and `requireCleanHead`, before fork push or `RecordCheckpoint`. Emit drift/skip information before publication; after obtaining the PR number print the mode-specific recovery command defined below for conflicts. Append the same numbered note to the PR body using `UpdateDraftPR` for newly created PRs and the known number for existing PRs. If the post-create advisory update fails, print the sanitized missing-note warning and exact recovery command, then continue to `RecordSubmission`; do not add retry repair. Preserve existing claim checks, remote-head fencing, validation failure behavior, and unchanged-base text.
4. Add only an additive `base_freshness` JSON object to the newly completed issue-submit success output with `status` (`unchanged`, `clean`, `conflicts`, `skipped`), nullable `base_drift` and `behind_count`, and an always-array `conflicted_paths`; optionally include pinned target SHA and sanitized skip reason. Use nulls for unknown values, never zeros that imply success. Keep JSON stdout parseable and send advisories to stderr in JSON mode. Leave the entire completed-path branch (`internal/cli/submit.go:89–106`) unchanged, including text and JSON: no freshness recomputation, new key, PR update, or publication. Existing label projection is retained. AC1 means byte-identical human text output when tip equals `base_sha`; for a new submission JSON keeps all existing fields and adds only `base_freshness`, as required by AC4.
5. Add the acceptance tests in TEST_PLAN.md, update both documentation files with informational behavior and the real recovery command, then run the required checks. Make no protected-path edits and no automatic rebases, approval changes, or changes to `swarm pr submit`.

## Exact conflict guidance

Substitute the actual PR number and selected remote name in these literal command forms:

- Same repository: `swarm pr rebase <PR> --resolve`.
- Fork with default remote `fork`: `swarm --fork pr rebase <PR> --resolve`.
- Fork with a non-default remote: `swarm --fork --fork-remote <name> pr rebase <PR> --resolve`. Include `--fork-remote` only for a non-default remote, quoting a remote name if required for shell use.

Use the same conflicted paths, command, and short approval line in terminal output and the PR note: “The moved base needs approval re-pinned before or during rebase; fork contributors need a maintainer to run `swarm issue approve <issue>` upstream first.” Same-repository `--resolve` can re-pin eligible unchanged task/policy approval; other cases use explicit maintainer approval, releasing an active claim first as described in `docs/developer.md:223`. Submission itself never performs these recovery actions. Flag sources: `internal/cli/root.go:88`, `internal/cli/pr.go:250`; default remote: `internal/workspace/worktree.go:63`.

## Recommended follow-up WorkUnits

- Repair missing freshness guidance through completed-submit retry or `pr status`, with an explicit decision about description mutation.
- Add freshness reporting to `swarm pr submit`.

These follow-ups are outside this implementation. Preserve the completed-retry behavior documented in `docs/developer.md:179`.

# Test plan: issue submission base freshness

Use disposable repositories, bare local remotes, the local tracker, and existing GitHub/fork tracker fixtures; no live GitHub service or credentials are required. These checks are for implementation; this planning phase does not run the production suite.

| Acceptance criterion | Concrete verification |
| --- | --- |
| Target equals approved base; output unchanged | `TestSubmitFreshnessUnchanged`: compare first-submit stdout byte-for-byte with `Submitted draft PR #%d for issue #%d on %s (%s)\n` (`internal/cli/submit.go:193`), with no freshness warning or PR body addition. Compare the existing success JSON identity map (`:190–191`) plus only `base_freshness` = unchanged/false/0/empty array; existing fields and values stay identical. Repeated submit retains the literal already-submitted text and original JSON without the new key (`:101–105`). Assert published head and approved base remain identical to expected values. |
| Clean drift proceeds and prints behind count | `TestSubmitFreshnessCleanDrift`: advance target by two independent commits after approval; submit exact candidate successfully, assert count 2, clean advisory before publication, draft PR identity, unchanged candidate/base/approval. Include selected `--base` differing from default. |
| Conflicting drift proceeds, paths and exact recovery command in output and PR | `TestSubmitFreshnessConflicts`: independently edit the same files; assert successful draft creation, sorted conflicted paths, exact mode-specific command in output and saved description: `swarm pr rebase <actual-number> --resolve`, `swarm --fork pr rebase <actual-number> --resolve` for default remote `fork`, and `swarm --fork --fork-remote personal pr rebase <actual-number> --resolve` for non-default remote `personal`. Assert the short approval-repinning line and explicit maintainer `swarm issue approve <actual-issue>` guidance for forks. Cover new draft creation and existing draft update; no rebase/index/worktree mutation. |
| JSON includes drift, behind count, paths | `TestSubmitFreshnessJSON`: table of unchanged, clean, conflicts, skipped for newly completed submissions; completed retries keep their original JSON; decode entire stdout as JSON, retain identity fields, assert typed freshness object and empty arrays versus null unknown scalar values. Verify stderr advisories never corrupt stdout. |
| Fetch unavailable prints skipped and proceeds | `TestSubmitFreshnessFetchFailure`: preserve cached origin/HEAD and stale tracking ref, make remote unavailable, omit `--base`, and ensure successful publication with skipped message rather than stale clean/conflict data. Repeat with explicit `--base`. Use local coordination or tracker doubles so failure affects inspection only. A nonexistent target ref also skips. |
| Unit cases and `make check` pass | `TestSubmitFreshness*` helper and CLI cases cover all four outcomes; run focused suite, then required checks and `make check` below. |

Additional boundary cases within this feature:

- Exercise target calculation for GitHub and local trackers in same-repository and fork mode. In fork fixtures, advance origin while the writable fork stays unchanged, then reverse; only origin controls freshness. For local without a remote, advance the named local base branch. Reuse GitHub tracker overrides and the existing fork end-to-end fixture in `internal/cli/cli_test.go`.
- Parser cases: multiple conflicts, spaces/tabs/newlines and non-ASCII paths, renames/deletes, conflict exit 1 with stdout, unexpected exit 2, malformed records, missing history, and unsupported merge-tree. Failures report skipped, never clean. Different tip with zero new reachable commits reports drift truthfully.
- In `internal/gitcredential/environment_test.go`, place a sentinel custom merge driver in disposable Git configuration and attributes; `Command` for merge-tree must override discovered driver values to fixed `false` and recursive drivers to built-in `binary`, retain credential configuration and existing filter protections, and never execute the sentinel. Verify probe failures/oversized configuration prevent running merge-tree and yield skipped in CLI tests. The sentinel test is mandatory and must fail against old behavior. Verify no token, remote URL containing credentials, or absolute workspace path enters advisories/PR description. Keep credential regression tests intact.
- Observe submission order with tracker/runner spies: validation failure and changed candidate prevent inspection and publication; check runs before checkpoint push/record and draft creation. Assert claim fencing, head fencing, base SHA, approval digests, branch, HEAD, index, and files are preserved by inspection.
- Force the advisory PR update to fail: submission identity remains recorded, a sanitized warning explicitly says the PR description lacks the freshness note and includes the exact mode-specific recovery command, then submission succeeds. A completed retry stays byte-identical in text and JSON and makes no tracker writes beyond existing label projection; spy on tracker updates, inspection, pushes, and submission recording to prove no repair or recomputation occurs, even after the target moves again. Test this after both successful and failed initial description updates.

## Verification commands

```bash
go test ./internal/cli -run 'TestSubmitFreshness' -count=1
go test ./internal/gitcredential -count=1
go test ./internal/cli ./internal/gitcredential ./internal/tracker ./internal/workspace
unformatted=$(gofmt -s -l .); if [ -n "$unformatted" ]; then printf '%s\n' "$unformatted"; exit 1; fi
go build ./...
go vet ./...
go tool staticcheck ./...
go test ./...
make check
```

Review the documentation diff against `internal/cli/submit.go` and the `--resolve` flag registered in `internal/cli/pr.go:250`. Confirm new relative links/anchors resolve and extract any added Bash snippets for `bash -n`. Documentation should explain the behind count, informational conflicts, skipped checks, and the numbered recovery step in ordinary developer language.

Live GitHub publication is not required for acceptance testing. Tracker fixtures verify draft requests/updates and saved descriptions; a maintainer may optionally inspect the resulting hosted rendering during PR review. The target may move again after the pinned inspection; describe results as an observation at submit time, not a merge guarantee.

Keep additional parser/path cases as inexpensive table cases; an awkward nonessential fixture does not expand the WorkUnit or block implementing the four required outcomes. Description repair and freshness for `swarm pr submit` remain follow-up WorkUnits.
